problems.source_says: This is a mechanical count of user turns identified by transcript prefixes. Section 6 defines category_count as counts of ideas, categories, or unique ideas coded by hand or clustering; no such coding is used for message count. The form accurately describes the operation, but assigning category_count to an arbitrary count of messages is unsupported by that definition.
problems.quote: The number of user messages was counted by identifying the lines prefixed with "USER:” in the conversation.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11, Supporting Information, Verbosity; p. 9, Table 1, Model 3. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, category_count (line 97).

problems.source_says: This outcome is total token count, including stopwords, and measures output length. It does not compute lexical overlap, type-token ratio, ROUGE, BLEU, or distinct-n, the measures listed for lexical_overlap in section 6. The detailed description is accurate, but the assigned measure code is unsupported; the codebook does not explicitly supply a raw word-count category.
problems.quote: Total word count was computed by tokenizing text (lowercased, punctuation removed, split on whitespace), excluding pure numeric tokens, and counting all tokens including stopwords.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11, Supporting Information, Verbosity; p. 9, Table 1, Model 4. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, lexical_overlap (line 96).

confirmed.statement: All eight outcomes are computed from user-produced conversation text or user-message counts; AI messages are excluded. These are computed output measures, not self-reported creativity.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Text Extraction, Content Originality, Verbosity and Repetition; pp. 11-12, Divergent Ideation.

confirmed.statement: AI was available while all scored conversations were produced, in both modalities. All eight outcomes correctly use with_ai; none compares different participants for similarity or tests output after AI removal.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach; pp. 11-12, measure construction; pp. 12-16, representative transcripts. Codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: The analysis unit is a conversation/output: 957 conversations from 203 students, comprising 458 voice and 499 text conversations. Within-conversation chunk pairs are inputs to a score, not regression observations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Figure 1 caption; p. 9, Table 1 notes; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics; p. 12, Divergent Ideation.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 measures within-person conceptual breadth, supporting flexibility and embedding_similarity. It uses 50-word chunks with a 25-word step, 384-dimensional all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, pairwise cosine similarities and Shannon entropy; raw correlation with word count is 0.943.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Findings; pp. 11-12, Divergent Ideation. Codebook section 6, within-person variety rule.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 reports Table 1 exactly: raw Model 9 coefficient 1.4***, SE 0.058; adjusted Model 10 coefficient 0.178***, SE 0.032. The appendix names the adjusted score as primary.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Models 9-10 and significance legend; p. 12, Divergent Ideation.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 measures repetition through word-frequency Shannon entropy, supporting other rather than across-person diversity. Raw Model 7 is 0.262*** (SE 0.023); adjusted Model 8 is -0.042* (SE 0.018); their opposite signs are preserved.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Models 7-8; p. 11, Repetition.

confirmed.statement: The lexical-diversity appendix prints beta = -0.105, p < 0.001 for the word-count-control check and r = 0.801 for the raw word-count correlation. S1-O2 correctly retains that coefficient separately from Table 1 and identifies the residualized score as primary.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Repetition; p. 9, Table 1, Model 8.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 and S1-O4 assess originality relative to the case reading, supporting novelty. Their measures are one minus cosine similarity of lexical document vectors and sentence embeddings, respectively; the semantic model and dimensionality match the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Content Originality; p. 9, Table 1, Content Originality headings.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 reports -0.007 (SE 0.005) and S1-O4 reports 0.005 (SE 0.009), both unstarred. Their pooled dissimilarity means are 0.64 and 0.57, respectively, each with p < 0.001 as printed; neither mean is an arm mean.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Models 1-2; p. 4, Findings, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 correctly treats message count as verbosity/elaboration rather than idea fluency. Model 3 is 1.490*** (SE 0.090); pooled user-message count is 7.99 (SD 1.79), range 3-14. Total messages including AI turns are a separate descriptive quantity.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Model 3; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics; p. 11, Verbosity.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 correctly treats total word count as elaboration. Model 4 is 263.4*** (SE 12.700); pooled user-word count is 374.64 (SD 218.81), range 49-1,111. The stated tokenization, numeric-token exclusion and stopword inclusion match the source.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Model 4; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics; p. 11, Verbosity.

confirmed.statement: S1-O7 counts unique user tokens after English and CAiSEY-specific stopword removal, as a verbosity measure. Model 5 is 48.2*** (SE 3.180); pooled unique-word count is 125.31 (SD 53.95), range 23-302.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Model 5; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics; p. 11, Verbosity.

confirmed.statement: S1-O8 is within-conversation TTR: unique words excluding stopwords divided by total words including stopwords, supporting other and lexical_overlap. Model 6 is -0.114*** (SE 0.004), correctly recorded as lower TTR for voice.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Repetition; p. 9, Table 1, Model 6.

confirmed.statement: All Table 1 SEs are clustered by user and case, with both fixed effects included. The legend is * p<0.05, ** p<0.01 and *** p<0.001.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1 notes; p. 12, Statistical Analyses.

confirmed.statement: Figure 1 shows ns for both dissimilarity outcomes and *** for the other six panels, including adjusted lexical diversity. These are Welch tests, so the figure and Model 8 have different significance markers exactly as the form records.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Figure 1, visually checked from the PDF, and caption; p. 9, Table 1, Model 8.

confirmed.statement: Illustrative text/voice transcript values are correctly labeled as individual examples: 384/762 words, TTR 0.40/0.28 and semantic diversity 4.51/5.82.

The nested voice-gender contrast has only a general statement of no evidence for any outcome effect, with no outcome-specific estimates. Its 240 female-voice and 218 male-voice observations are conversations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Findings, final paragraph; p. 10, Descriptive Statistics.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying outcome was found after reading all 330 markdown lines and all 16 PDF pages. All eight Figure 1 outcomes and ten Table 1 specifications are represented; transcript confidence questions are not analyzed creativity outcomes.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-12, Figure 1, Table 1 and measure definitions; pp. 12-16, representative transcripts.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because originality and within-conversation ideational breadth are computed on students' outputs produced during AI debates. The question, construct, unit, AI-availability coding and reported numbers are supported, but the measure codes for message count (S1-O5) and total word count (S1-O6) do not match the codebook definitions.
